history.period: Late 20th century (stupa construction begun 1988; monastery established by Tibetan monks and followers of the Dalai Lama)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Buddhist monastery and stupa; keep-or-drop decision needed. Salugara Monastery is a Buddhist shrine on the outskirts of Siliguri, about 6 km from the city, founded by Tibetan monks and followers of the Dalai Lama. Its main attraction is the 100-foot Great International Tashi Gomang Stupa, commissioned by the Tibetan lama Kalu Rinpoche (construction begun 1988); the stupa holds five kinds of Buddhist relics and is highly revered. The complex has landscaped gardens and a meditation centre, and is maintained by the Droden Kunchab Chodey Buddhist Association.

town_description: Siliguri is the largest city of North Bengal and the main gateway to the Northeast, Sikkim, Bhutan and Nepal. Straddling the Darjeeling and Jalpaiguri districts on the banks of the Mahananda river, it grew from a small trading town into a busy commercial and transport hub, served by Bagdogra airport and the New Jalpaiguri and Siliguri Junction railway stations.
